title: Kabsa (Saudi Spiced Chicken and Rice with Raisins and Almonds)
summary: Salted chicken browned, then cooked with spiced rice, tomato, carrot, bay, dried lime and orange zest until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C. Topped with fried almonds, pine nuts and raisins and served with fresh tomato daqqus.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dried lime (loomi), pierced, or a strip of lime peel
basmati rice, washed until the water runs clear
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Season and brown
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and rub it with the salt, leaving it for 30 min if you have time so it seasons deeply. Heat the ghee in the Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the pieces skin side down in two batches for 5-7 min until well coloured, then set aside.

steps.title: Build the spice base
steps.text: Cook the onion in the chicken fat over medium heat for 5 min until lightly golden. Add the garlic, ginger, tomato paste and spices and stir for 1 min until very fragrant; frying ground spices briefly in fat brings out their aroma.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Stir in the tomatoes, carrot, bay, loomi and orange zest and cook for 4 min, scraping the base, until jammy. Add the rice and stir for 2 min, then pour in the water and add the salt.

steps.title: Cook together
steps.text: Nestle the chicken in skin side up and bring to the boil. Cover and cook on low for 25-28 min, until the rice is tender, a light crust has formed underneath and the chicken reaches 74 °C. Rest covered off the heat for 10 min.

steps.title: Topping and daqqus
steps.text: Meanwhile, fry the almonds in the oil for 1 min, add the pine nuts for 1 min more, then the raisins until they plump; tip into a bowl. Stir together the diced tomato, garlic, chilli, lemon juice and pinch of salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fluff the rice onto a large platter, arrange the chicken on top and scatter over the nut and raisin mixture. Serve with the daqqus on the side.

tips: Wash the rice well so the grains stay long and separate.
Dried lime gives a gentle sour, musky note; find it in Middle Eastern shops.
A spoonful of yoghurt alongside cools the spices.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat covered with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C). Keep the daqqus separately for up to 1 day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
